title: Say what the solver found before reading a plan

blocks.text: A dispatch team (not GridCap) runs CP-SAT models of many shapes from one service, and the service has to tell its callers what came back. Last week it returned "plan: []" for a model the solver had refused, and the caller read that as "load nothing".

Write `report(model, x, solver=None)` in `report.py`. `x` maps names to the model's Boolean variables; `solver` is a `CpSolver` the caller may have configured (make a new one when it is `None`). Solve the model once and return a dict with five keys:

rows: the sorted names whose Boolean is true, when the status carries a solution; else `None`
the objective value rounded to an `int`, when there is a solution *and* the model has an objective; else `None`
`True` only when the solution was proved best
for an invalid model, the solver's explanation of what is wrong; else `""`

blocks.text: Use the lesson's table of the five statuses to decide which ones carry a solution. `model.has_objective()` says whether an objective was set. The tests build small models of each kind, including a search the caller stops at its first plan. About twelve lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

from report import report


def boxes(capacity):
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    x = {name: model.new_bool_var(name) for name in ("ice", "fish", "bread", "fruit")}
    model.add(3 * x["ice"] + 5 * x["fish"] + 2 * x["bread"] + 4 * x["fruit"] <= capacity)
    model.maximize(4 * x["ice"] + 7 * x["fish"] + 2 * x["bread"] + 5 * x["fruit"])
    return model, x


solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
solver.parameters.max_time_in_seconds = 10
print("capacity 9:", report(*boxes(9), solver))

model, x = boxes(9)
model.add(x["ice"] + x["fish"] >= 3)
print("capacity 9, three of two:", report(model, x))

model, x = boxes(9)
model.add(x["ice"] + x["fish"] <= 1).only_enforce_if(model.new_int_var(0, 3, "count"))
print("enforced by an integer:", report(model, x))

cases.says: a proven optimum gives its status, its plan, its objective and proven = True
an infeasible model gives its status and no plan and no objective
a search stopped at its first plan still gives that plan, marked not proven
an invalid model gives no plan and the solver's own reason
a model with no objective gives a plan and no objective value

origin.section: Read the Status Before You Read a Value

concepts: a CP-SAT program builds a CpModel, solves it with a CpSolver and checks the status before reading values
only OPTIMAL and FEASIBLE carry a solution, and only OPTIMAL proves it best
